stem: After tonsillectomy, a patient has reduced taste and general sensation over the posterior third of the tongue. Tongue movement is normal. Which nerve was most likely injured?

options.label: A
options.explanation: It carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, rather than the posterior third.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Its taste fibres serve the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and travel with the lingual nerve.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It supplies most tongue muscles; injury would produce motor weakness rather than this taste and sensory pattern.

options.label: D
options.text: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
options.explanation: It supplies sensation above the vocal folds and the epiglottic region, rather than the posterior-third tongue territory.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Its proximity to the tonsillar bed makes it vulnerable during tonsillectomy; it carries taste and general sensation from the posterior third of the tongue.

context: The glossopharyngeal nerve runs close to the tonsillar bed and carries posterior-tongue sensation and taste. Preserved movement helps distinguish this sensory deficit from hypoglossal injury.
